question: Can integrated gradients be extended inside a fine-tuned protein transformer to identify residue-level and head-specific signals that align with independent biological annotations?

key_findings.claim: The paper computes head-specific residue attributions by integrating from the embedding layer through an attention block.
key_findings.evidence: A common straight path is fixed in embedding space, producing a generally curved intermediate path; multi-head output dimensions are separated, and the skip-connection contribution is excluded before summing model dimensions per head.

key_findings.claim: Embedding-level attributions align with some, but not all, expected annotations.
key_findings.evidence: GO membrane relevance correlates strongly with transmembrane regions, whereas GO catalytic-activity and binding cases do not show the analogous embedding-level signal. For EC prediction, five of six main classes correlate with active and binding sites.

key_findings.claim: The statistical head maps go beyond isolated examples but do not prove that a head implements a biological concept.
key_findings.evidence: Per-protein point-biserial correlations are tested over 480 layer-head cells with Wilcoxon tests and false-discovery correction, then masked by positive summed relevance. Correlation and decodability remain weaker evidence than causal intervention.

key_findings.claim: A residue-substitution sanity check supports attribution faithfulness at the aggregate level.
key_findings.evidence: Replacing the 64 most relevant residues with alanine reduces EC accuracy from 0.9898 to 0.8677, versus 0.9296 for random residues; intermediate replacement counts show the same ordering.

anchors.section: Table E.4 and XAI evaluation with residue substitution

key_findings.claim: End-to-end fine-tuning improves prediction, while much attribution structure already exists in the pretrained encoder.
key_findings.evidence: For EC50 L1, full fine-tuning reaches 0.990 accuracy versus 0.829 with a frozen encoder and 0.369 after parameter shuffling; significant-head overlap is 0.43 between tuned and frozen pretrained variants but about 0.035 with shuffled weights.

anchors.section: On pretraining and finetuning from end-to-end

method.core_idea: Use class-conditioned path attributions inside each attention head and validate their residue maps against external sequence annotations across a protein population.
method.mechanism: Fine-tune ProtBert/ProtT5/ESM-2 on GO and EC labels, compute integrated gradients per head and residue, correlate them with UniProt/PROSITE annotations, correct multiple tests, and perturb top-attributed residues.
assumptions: The embedding baseline and path are biologically meaningful
Database annotations are sufficiently complete and independent
A head's sliced output dimensions isolate its contribution
Alanine substitutions are a valid perturbation control

techniques.role: Attributes a class score to residues separately for every transformer head.
Aggregates head-map alignment across proteins while correcting many tests.
Tests whether highly attributed residues are more causally important than random residues.

evaluations.setting: ProtBert fine-tuned for GO membrane/catalytic/binding terms and six EC classes
evaluations.metric: head relevance, residue-annotation correlation, FDR-adjusted Wilcoxon tests
evaluations.result: multiple class- and annotation-specific significant heads; strongest embedding-level GO result is membrane/transmembrane
evaluations.baseline: pretrained/frozen and shuffled encoders plus unrelated annotations

evaluations.setting: EC50 L1 test proteins with alanine substitution
evaluations.result: 64 relevant substitutions yield 0.8677 versus 0.9296 for random and 0.9898 unmodified

limitations: Head attribution correlation does not establish a mechanistic computation.
Only ProtBert is analyzed deeply because larger models are expensive.
Annotation incompleteness and sequence homology can confound alignment.
The curved hidden-state path sacrifices the straight-path symmetry axiom of standard integrated gradients.
The approach requires a class-specific prediction head.
failure_modes: A baseline off the protein manifold creates misleading gradients.
A head correlates with hydrophobicity rather than membrane function itself.
Redundant heads make single-head interpretation unstable across runs.
reusable_insights: Validate biological attributions at population scale against external residue annotations.
Pair correlation tests with targeted perturbation, randomization, and frozen-model controls.
Report both positive and null biological concepts to avoid cherry-picking.
open_questions: Do identified heads remain stable across seeds, architectures, and homology-controlled splits?
Can patching or head ablation distinguish causal specialization from correlated encoding?
Can unexplained attribution motifs predict experimentally verifiable function?

competitive_landscape.title: BERTology Meets Biology: Interpreting Attention in Protein Language Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Vig et al. inspect raw attention for contacts, binding sites, and biophysical properties across architectures; this paper uses class-conditioned integrated gradients inside a fine-tuned predictor with population statistics and perturbation checks.

competitive_landscape.title: ProtTrans: Towards Cracking the Language of Life's Code Through Self-Supervised Deep Learning and High Performance Computing
competitive_landscape.difference: ProtTrans establishes large protein language models and strong transferred representations; the reviewed work fine-tunes ProtBert/ProtT5 and asks where class evidence resides.

competitive_landscape.title: Axiomatic Attribution for Deep Networks
competitive_landscape.difference: Sundararajan et al. define integrated gradients for input features along a straight path; this work adapts it to intermediate head outputs while fixing the path upstream in embedding space.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The work supplies first quantitative evidence that internal protein-transformer attribution maps correspond to sequence annotations across many proteins.
novelty_assessment.evidence: Head-resolved IG, corrected population tests, model randomization, and alanine replacement produce convergent evidence.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The population-scale protocol is a real advance over anecdotal attention maps, but 'specialized heads' should be read as statistically aligned components until causal circuit tests and homology controls are added.

reviewer_notes: Read the 26-page extraction including supplement, with a second pass on path construction, test corrections, null results, fine-tuning controls, and alanine substitution. Primary competitor records were checked on arXiv.
